The verdict comes from rendered frames only.. Judge: B wins all four pairs. Pairs 1-3 are decisive; pair 4 is close but still clear. The A frames are credible at the environment level: warm low-sun lighting with long shadows, region-specific architecture (shophouses, colonnades, encaustic tiles, a twin-tower skyline), sculpted rain trees and high crowd counts. In the wide street shot (pair 4) this almost competes. But every character-led A frame breaks down on the human. Skin is plastic or clay with no pore or specular breakup, hair is a solid helmet, and the shirt is a flat plaid texture with no cloth folds. Poses are stiff and symmetric with claw hands. Props are held by the fingertips or clip into clothing, the feet are weakly grounded, crowd models and walk cycles are cloned, and no character performs a story beat. Building interiors are black voids. The B frames win through authored acting: expressions and gaze, garment layering and folds, natural grips with weight, and props that imply a narrative (a jerry can beside a burning car, a bat, leaning on a car). They also win on grounded contact shadows and on pedestrians who do varied things together. Suggested fix order for A: (1) fidelity of the main character: skin shader, hair cards, cloth normal detail, and hand IK and grip poses for held props; (2) contact shadows and ambient occlusion at the feet, plus weight-shifted idle poses; (3) more varied crowd behavior and fewer duplicated models; (4) fill shop openings with interiors, signage and props, and put moving traffic on the roads.
